Definition: from G2330 (in the sense of the crop); to harvest:--reap.
BiblicalUsage: The word therízō is the Bible's way of saying to reap, to harvest. In Matthew 6:26, neither do they reap. That is the sense it carries through all 17 of its occurrences.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that sowing and reaping is God’s honest order, and I will reap what I have sown, for good or for ill. That is why I read the passages around therízō slowly, instead of hurrying past.
